tagline: First spacecraft to encounter Saturn — Jupiter flyby in 1974 then gravity-assist to Saturn in 1979
description: Spin-stabilised RTG-powered probe (~259 kg), sibling of Pioneer 10 with the same bus and Pioneer Plaque message-to-the-stars. Launched 1973-04-06 on an Atlas SLV-3D Centaur D-1A + Star-37E from Cape Canaveral. Jupiter flyby 1974-12-03 at 43 000 km — the closest of any Pioneer encounter, returned the first polar-region images and the gravity assist needed to reach Saturn. Saturn encounter 1979-09-01 at 21 000 km from the cloud tops — first detailed images of the ring system, discovery of a new ring (F-ring) and a new moon, confirmation of Saturn's nearly-aligned magnetic field. Continued outbound observations until last contact 1995-11-24. Now ~93 AU from the Sun, headed toward Aquila.
best_known_for: First spacecraft to encounter Saturn — 1979-09-01 flyby, sibling to Pioneer 10
